title: Roman missal states: bounded book and component revisions

traditions.label: Roman-curial missal and ceremonial witnesses
traditions.scope: Latin curial books and bounded ceremonial components before the 1570 Roman Missal revision.
traditions.coverage_note: An attested printed witness does not establish a direct ancestor of the 1570 recension.

traditions.label: Roman Missal: 1570–1962 editions and later supplements
traditions.scope: The 1570 recension and its later revisions, including complementary Holy Week books and the 1962 Canon amendment. The 2020 optional-preface supplement is separately bounded.
traditions.coverage_note: Intervening calendar, rubrical and printed states are incomplete; no century-long identical text is inferred.

traditions.label: Postconciliar Latin Roman Missal
traditions.scope: Original Latin reform and typical-edition states, with companion lectionary distinguished from the altar book.
traditions.coverage_note: Independent vernacular histories are deferred. 1969 legislation, 1970 complete book and 2000 approval/2002 printing retain separate roles.

sources.title: Lippe, Missale Romanum Mediolani 1474, volume I (1899)
sources.inspection: Read rendered PDF 11 (preface), 15 (introduction ix), 35 (edited opening p 1); inspected explanatory text PDF 13–15.
sources.limitations: A critical edition, not direct examination of the 1474 copy; editorial additions and supplied lacunae are distinguishable.

sources.title: Legg, Tracts on the Mass (1904)
sources.inspection: Read page images of printed xxvi–xxvii, PDF 34–35, identifying 1501 and 1502 recensions and concrete expansion; earlier review read comparative notes 249–250.
sources.limitations: Scholarly comparison, not new full collation. Do not repeat the outdated claim that 1502 was the first standalone edition.

sources.title: Maura O’Carroll, Dominican Liturgy in the Thirteenth Century (1979)
sources.inspection: Previously inspected rendered article pp 80–84 and pericope comparisons in this research lane; cites Haymo presentation 1243 and critical editions.
sources.limitations: Exact Haymo manuscript-state and implementation remain unestablished here.

sources.title: Pałęcki, Carthusian Mass comparison (2015)
sources.inspection: Previously inspected printed 114 n 22 and 120–122; exact Rome 1570 Faletti/Varisco comparator and bounded Canon differences.
sources.limitations: Original 1570 Rome copy not independently acquired; no full Roman/medieval collation.

sources.title: Missale Romanum, Rome: Typographia Vaticana 1604
sources.inspection: Downloaded original scan for research; page images PDF 5 title and 9 Cum sanctissimum read.
sources.limitations: Google digitization research-only; no new retained-publication permission inferred. Constitution describes correction policy, not an exhaustive before/after apparatus.

sources.title: Urban VIII, Si quid est (1634), reprinted in 1962 missal
sources.inspection: Read page image PDF 6: revision description and 2 September 1634 dateline.
sources.limitations: Later facsimile witness of the act; original 1634 book not examined.

sources.title: Decretum approbationis editionis typicae Vaticanae (1920), in 2004 reprint
sources.inspection: Read rendered PDF 3, printed 3*, including 1900 baseline, appendix and 25 July 1920 dateline.
sources.limitations: This is the identified 2004 Bonn Aedibus Palmarum reimpressio, not an original 1920 printing. Its bibliographic identity is canonical; no proof all body readings equal 1920.

sources.title: Maxima redemptionis nostrae mysteria, AAS 47 (1955) 838–841
sources.inspection: Downloaded official PDF and read page images 838–841, including §§ 1–2 and 6–9.
sources.limitations: Describes prescribed Holy Week state and effective date; complete 1956 service book not transcribed or page-collated here.

sources.title: John XXIII, Rubricarum instructum (25 July 1960)
sources.inspection: Read official Latin HTML, especially numbered 1–6 and dateline.
sources.limitations: Approves/replaces rubrical corpus; individual rubrical differences require code comparison.

sources.title: Missale Romanum 1962: June decree and later amended Canon in the available Vatican facsimile
sources.inspection: Read decree image PDF 2 and front-matter headings via text locator; source identity is existing canonical Vatican facsimile, not Benziger. Rendered printed p. 302/PDF 383 also inspected: the Communicantes already includes Joseph.
sources.limitations: Decree itself prints 23 July 1960 when referring to Rubricarum instructum; official act is 25 July. No silent correction. June book and later Canon amendment separated. This digital witness’s Canon is consequently not an unchanged June 1962 body; its retained June decree attests that earlier approval, while its body witnesses the subsequent amendment. Exact impression date remains unestablished.

sources.title: SCR, De S.Ioseph nomine Canoni Missae inserendo, AAS 54 (1962) 873
sources.inspection: Read original official page image 873: 13 November decree, 8 December effective date, insertion and proper Communicantes rule.
sources.limitations: Amendment to a book state, not a separate complete missal printing.

sources.title: Paul VI, Missale Romanum (3 April 1969)
sources.inspection: Read official constitution, new Eucharistic Prayers, Order, readings, propers and 30 November 1969 effective clause.
sources.limitations: English official translation used for description of Latin reform, not copied as prayer text; no territorial implementation inference.

sources.title: Missale Romanum, editio typica tertia 2002, constituent decrees
sources.inspection: Downloaded existing identified secondary digitally typeset witness; page images PDF 2–3 read for 1975 and third-edition decrees; title/publication list and 1970 decree read in PDF text. Also inspected rendered PDF 370, Ordo Missae § 144, for the existing dismissal formula.
sources.limitations: Secondary reproduction, not original printed page scan. 2000 approval/decree and stated effective clause are not 2002 publication; no full modern body import.

sources.title: Notitiae 44 (2008) 503–504, reprint notice and variations
sources.inspection: Downloaded official PDF; read page images 49–50, printed 367–368, for status and bounded changes.
sources.limitations: Official contemporaneous notice/list, not complete 2008 altar book. Only named changes, no exhaustive text collation.

sources.title: Paternas vices: Latin decree dated 1 May 2013, published 19 June 2013
sources.inspection: Read original Latin section, especially Exinde and Circa textus paragraphs, dateline and bulletin publication header.
sources.limitations: Describes exact amendment; no complete 2013 altar-book impression examined.

sources.title: Quo magis: Latin decree and seven-preface annex
sources.inspection: Read Latin decree and all seven annex sections, including their use rubrics; official HTML.
sources.limitations: Supplementary texts, not a new complete missal; no modern prayer bodies imported.

sources.title: Official explanatory note on the seven additional prefaces
sources.inspection: Read paragraphs on optional use, four postconciliar sources, three formerly local prefaces, and retained earlier concessions.
sources.limitations: Official explanation of repertoire and scope; no exact donor-edition collation or claim of newly composed prayers.

stages.label: Haymo-associated missal ordinal
stages.scope: Ordinal redaction, not a whole surviving uniform missal.
stages.witness_label: Ordo Missalis associated with Haymo; critical editions cited by O’Carroll
stages.summary: Reported chapter presentation of the Franciscan-curial ordinal.

evidence.claim: 1243 presentation and critical-edition identification.

stages.limitations: Exact component redaction, authorship and community implementation require further witness study.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Printed Roman-curial missal
stages.scope: Identified 1474 printed witness mediated by critical edition.
stages.witness_label: Milan 1474, Ambrosiana S.Q.N.III.14 as described in Lippe 1899
stages.summary: Opening expressly names Roman-curial use; contains Mass propers and Canon.

evidence.claim: Identifies 1474 copy and Roman-curial opening.

stages.limitations: Not Ambrosian rite. Critical publication 1899 is not state date; supplied lacunae and expanded abbreviations are editorial. No direct Haymo → 1474 or 1474 → 1570 parent asserted.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Short Burchard ceremonial
stages.summary: Shorter Ordo Missae recension within a Roman missal.

evidence.claim: Exact printer/copy and shorter recension identified.

stages.limitations: Separate from 1501 Giunta; no claim of a universally promulgated whole-missal revision.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Expanded Burchard ceremonial
stages.summary: Expanded Ordo Missae with substantial added directions.

evidence.claim: 1502 text expanded relative to 1501; explicit examples.

stages.limitations: Not a complete missal; not claimed first standalone Burchard edition; not proven sole parent of Pian Ritus.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Roman Missal revised under Pius V
stages.scope: The promulgated Roman recension, anchored to an identified early printing.
stages.witness_label: Rome 1570, heirs of Bartolomeo Faletti, Joannes Variscus and associates
stages.summary: Roman Missal revised under Pius V with ordered ceremonial and Roman Canon.

evidence.claim: Identified 1570 book and Canon comparator.
Recites the Pian missal as the book being revised.

stages.limitations: 14 July 1570 Quo primum is an act date, not claimed exact printing day; no full textual delta from 1474 proven. Exempt older uses are not silently incorporated.
stages.reception: Roman use subject to Quo primum and its exemptions; no assertion that every Latin use was replaced.

stages.label: Clementine corrected missal
stages.scope: Vatican recension documented by its actual title and prefatory explanation.
stages.summary: Corrected textual transmission and fuller, clearer ritual rules.

evidence.claim: Book identity and emendation rationale.

stages.limitations: 7 July 1604 approval distinct from imprint year. Corrections described by the act, not enumerated here line by line; do not say all liturgical quotations were newly conformed to Vulgate.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Urbanian corrected missal
stages.scope: Book recension described in its issuing constitution.
stages.witness_label: Missale Romanum ordered for publication under Urban VIII; original 1634 copy not inspected
stages.summary: Clarified/restored rubrics and correction of scriptural divergences against Vulgate.

evidence.claim: Names prior revisions and describes corrections.

stages.limitations: 2 September 1634 is approval/instrument date. Later reprint witnesses the description, not every 1634 reading; no original 1634 title-page check.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Missal revised under Pius X and Benedict XV
stages.scope: Identifiable typical-book state; exact original printing not acquired.
stages.witness_label: Vatican typical edition 1920, described by decree reproduced in 2004 Bonn reprint
stages.summary: 1900 baseline adapted to recent prescriptions and Breviary revisions; appendix of approved local Masses.

evidence.claim: 1900 baseline and specific appendix described; 25 July 1920 approval.

stages.limitations: Neither later composite nor 2004 reprint is an original 1920 impression. 1634 → 1920 is not a proven single transition; intervening editions and prescriptions remain gaps.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Reformed Holy Week component
stages.scope: Complementary Ordo Hebdomadae Sanctae Instauratus replacing Holy Week order within Roman usage.
stages.witness_label: Vatican typical restored Holy Week order specified by Maxima redemptionis
stages.summary: Triduum moved from morning observance to prescribed evening/afternoon/night times.

evidence.claim: Prescribes revised Ordo and 25 March 1956 commencement.

stages.limitations: Approval 16 November 1955; effective 25 March 1956. Not an entire 1955/1956 Missale Romanum. Exact service-book printing and full prayer changes need inspection.
stages.reception: Roman rite follows revised Ordo; other Latin rites bound by celebration times only, per § 1.

stages.label: Typical missal with new rubrical code
stages.scope: Whole missal accommodating 1960 code; Holy Week reform is a component.
stages.witness_label: June 1962 typical-book state attested by its decree, retained in the available later-amended Vatican facsimile
stages.summary: New general and missal rubrics replace older front-matter code and additions.

evidence.claim: New edition explicitly accommodated to new code.
Code effective 1 January 1961; new editions replace old rubric sections.

stages.limitations: The June state is not automatically the later December Canon state. Holy Week incorporation is not a fresh full-book collation. Code approval on 25 July 1960 differs from the mistyped 23 July reference in the 1962 decree. No existing target-1962 text projection is bound to this specifically June state. The available facsimile already includes Joseph at printed p. 302/PDF 383, so it does not supply an unchanged June Canon witness.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Canon with St Joseph inserted
stages.scope: Single amendment to 1962 Canon, including proper Communicantes forms.
stages.witness_label: 1962 Missal amended by De S.Ioseph nomine Canoni Missae inserendo
stages.summary: St Joseph is named after the Blessed Virgin before the Apostles in Communicantes.

evidence.claim: Exact insertion, extension and 8 December effective date.
The inspected facsimile body contains Joseph at the location prescribed by the November decree; its exact impression date is not established.

stages.limitations: Decree 13 November 1962, effective 8 December 1962. Not a separately identified complete printing; no new full Canon transcription. The inspected facsimile confirms the amended reading, but is not dated precisely enough to establish when that particular impression appeared.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Reformed Order and first complete typical missal
stages.date_label: 1970 complete typical missal; 1969 Order and reform separately dated
stages.scope: Complete 1970 altar-book state, incorporating the 1969 Order and reform; the complementary reading system remains distinguished.
stages.witness_label: Ordo Missae 1969 and Missale Romanum editio typica 1970; complementary publications in one reform state
stages.summary: Revised Order, expanded Eucharistic Prayer repertoire and seasonal propers; multi-year readings in companion system.

evidence.claim: Describes concrete reform; 30 November 1969 effective.

evidence.locus: PDF 1 title/publication list and Celebrationis eucharisticae
evidence.claim: 1970 complete typical edition; 26 March 1970 decree.

stages.limitations: Approval on 3 April 1969 and the reform’s effective date of 30 November 1969 are distinct from publication of the complete book in 1970. The 1965, 1967 and 1968 intermediate changes remain unrepresented; this is a cumulative state, not a claim that every innovation first appeared in 1970. Native Latin scope; no English translation history.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Second typical missal with revised ministries and propers
stages.scope: Second complete Latin typical edition as described by its issuing decree.
stages.summary: Revises ministry descriptions and supplements ritual/votive formularies.

evidence.claim: Enumerated revisions; decree 27 March 1975.

stages.limitations: Complete 1975 altar-book witness not acquired; decree reprinted in 2002 proves bounded changes, not whole-book collation.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Third typical missal with expanded prayers and instruction
stages.witness_label: Missale Romanum, editio typica tertia, Typis Vaticanis 2002
stages.summary: Expanded General Instruction, new formularies and daily Lenten prayers over the people.

evidence.claim: Approval 10 April 2000; decree 20 April 2000; 2002 publication; listed changes.
The inspected Order of Mass includes the Ite, missa est dismissal before the additional options described in the 2008 notice.

stages.limitations: Retain printed decree’s 2000 effective-date statement separately; do not infer complete book availability in 2000. Secondary digital witness; no full modern corpus import.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Emended third-edition reprint
stages.scope: Bounded emendations to 2002 book, not a fourth typical edition.
stages.witness_label: Missale Romanum, reimpressio emendata 2008, evidenced by official notice/list
stages.summary: Omits children’s Eucharistic Prayers from Latin volume; allows dismissal alternatives and amends rubrics.

evidence.claim: Contemporaneous explicit reprint status and named substantive amendments.

stages.limitations: Complete 2008 altar book not acquired. Notice cites 8 June 2008 approval for selected changes; no exact printing day established. Typographic corrections are not all substantive.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Joseph added to Eucharistic Prayers II–IV
stages.scope: Latin Eucharistic Prayers II, III and IV of the third typical edition only.

stages.summary: Adds Joseph after Mary in the saints’ commemorations.

evidence.locus: Latin Exinde and Circa textus paragraphs; dateline
evidence.claim: Joseph is inserted after Mary in Eucharistic Prayers II, III and IV; these Latin formulas become typical.

stages.limitations: A component amendment, not a newly identified complete printing. The decree says henceforth; no separate exact effective day is inferred from its publication date.
stages.reception: Latin Roman text; vernacular approval histories remain separate.

stages.label: Seven optional prefaces supplement the 1962 missal
stages.scope: Supplemental preface repertoire: Angels, John the Baptist, Martyrs, All Saints and Patrons, Blessed Sacrament, Church Dedication, and Marriage.

evidence.locus: Decree operative paragraph and annex headings/rubrics

evidence.locus: Paragraphs beginning Four of the newly approved texts and As indicated
evidence.claim: Four texts derive from the postconciliar missal; three previously had local French/Belgian authorization. Use remains optional.

stages.limitations: Papal approval dated 5 December 2019 is distinct from the 2020 decree and effective date. Not a whole-missal printing, mandatory replacement, or seven newly composed texts.
stages.reception: Describes the 2020 supplement for the 1962 use; no present-day permission judgment or universal actual uptake claimed.
